newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli leader may see Jordan's king in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Israeli leader may see Jordan's king in U.S.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu may meet Jordan's King Hussein in the United States next week before going to the White House to meet U.S. President Bill Clinton, an Israeli spokesman said on Thursday.

"There is a possibility that at the request of Hussein the prime minister will go to visit him at the Minnesota hospital where he is having surgery on the way from Israel to Washington," an official at Netanyahu's office told Reuters.

The Israeli leader will meet Clinton in the U.S. capital on Monday, part of a U.S. bid to save Middle East peace moves plunged into a crisis and clashes following Netanyahu's groundbreaking on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Israel Radio said Netanyahu could discuss with the king the fate of Mousa Mohammed Abu Marzook, a leader of the militant Palestinian group Hamas who is jailed in the United States.
Israeli and U.S. officials have been trying to find ways to avoid extraditing Abu Marzook to Israel -- perhaps sending him to Jordan instead.

Israel and Jordan are partners to a 1994 peace treaty but the Jewish state's relations with the Arab world have been tense since Netanyahu started work last month at the site Israelis call Har Homa and the Arabs call Jabal Abu Ghneim.
The hilltop site is at the edge of East Jerusalem, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war from Jordan and claimed by both Israelis and Palestinians as their own.
